en: Udāna 6.10 Uppajjanti-sutta Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, as long as Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise in the world,
wanderers of other sects are honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated, and they receive gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings,
and medicinal requisites for the sick. But when, venerable sir, Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones arise in the world, then those wanderers of other sects...”
“The wanderers are now unhonored, unvenerated, not esteemed, not worshipped, and not respected; they do not receive gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.

But now, Bhante, it is the Blessed One alone who is honored, venerated, esteemed, worshipped, and respected, and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus as well, receiving gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
“It is so, Ānanda. It is even so, Ānanda: as long as Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise in the world...”
At that time, Ānanda, the wanderers of other sects were honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and respected,
and they received gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. But when Tathāgatas, Arhats,
Perfectly Enlightened Ones arise in the world, then [the gains of] the wanderers of other sects [diminish].
“The wanderers have become unhonored, unesteemed, uncared for, unworshipped, and unvenerated; they do not receive gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.

But now it is the Tathāgata who is honored, esteemed, cared for, worshipped, and venerated, and so too is the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, receiving gains of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“That glow-worm shines only so long as the light-maker has not risen; once the sun has appeared,
[the glow-worm’s light is gone].”
His radiance fades and he does not speak;
such is the mere illumination of the logicians,
as long as the Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise in the world.
“Neither the logicians nor their disciples are purified;
those of wrong view are not released from suffering.
Thus ends the tenth [verse].
Its summary verse:
Āyu, Jaṭila, Veckhana,
the three sectarians, and Subhūti.
The courtesan was the ninth;
and ten such arise.
This is the sixth chapter, the Chapter on the Born Blind.
